Heard on I.A. No.19952 of 2024,
which is an application for compromise filed by the complainant.
2. On perusal of the application, it is revealed that it does not bear the signature of the applicant/accused as he is in jail.
3. Vide this Court order dated 31.08.2024, complainant was directed to remain present before the Registrar (J-II) of this Court on 26.09.2024 for recording his statements.
Registrar (J-II) after recording the statements of the complainant has submitted verification report and has reported that compromise has been done without any threat, inducement or pressure.

2 CRR-3058-2024 4. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused has submitted that as parties have entered into compromise and complainant (respondent herein) has also filed an application for compromise,
therefore, it is prayed that compromise application may be allowed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties and the applicant/accused may be acquitted of the offence.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the applicant/accused and has submitted that the offences under Section 457 and 380 of IPC is not compoundable under two tables of under Section 320 of Cr.P.C.

Learned counsel for the complainant has admitted the factum of compromise between the parties and has prayed for Pankaj Hada vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128596002/
1 allowing the compromise application.
6.

Vs.
Pankaj Hada ) by learned Jucicial Magistrate First Class, Ashta, District Sehore (MP).

8. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the order dated 13.02.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.3853 of 2024 ( Shivam @ Siddarth Vs. State of MP & another ) by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, Bench at Indore, whereby, an application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. was allowed and FIR registered at Crime No.452/2020 of Police Station Vijay Nagar, District Indore for commission of offence under Section 363, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of IPC, Section 5(I), 6, 5(J)(ii) of the 4 CRR-3058-2024 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and the consequential proceedings in S.T. No.46/2020 pending before the Court of Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Indore were quashed and the applicant/accused therein was acquitted of the offence in view of the compromise arrived at between the parties.
9.

sentences.text: As far the powers conferred under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and the proceedings of the non-compoundable offences under Section 320 of Cr.P.C. are concerned, both are different.
An offence which is not compoundable under any of the table under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., cannot be compounded as Legislature has not mentioned the same in both the tables.

10. Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of State of MP Vs. Laxmi Narayan; (2019) 5 SCC 688, has held as under:-
"15.1

entities.text: State of MP Vs. Laxmi Narayan; (2019) 5 SCC 688
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
That the power conferred under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings for the non- compoundable offences under Section 320 of the Code can be exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character,
particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst themselves;
5 CRR-3058-2024 15.2 Such power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involved heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder,
rape, dacoity, etc.

Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society."

2

entities.text: Pankaj Hada vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11 . Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Murali Vs. State; (2021) 1 SCC 726, has held that the unequivocal language of Sub-Clause 9 of Section 320 of Cr.P.C. explicitly prohibits any compounding except as permitted under Section 320 of Cr.P.C.

Notwithstanding thereto, the factum of amicable settlement/compromise arrived at between the parties can be a relevant fact for the purpose of reduction in the quantum of sentence; even in serious non-compoundable offence.

12. Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Unnikrishnan Vs. State of Kerala; 2018 (15) SCC 343 has held that if an offence is not compoundable within the Code under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., Court may in view of the compromise arrived at between the parties, reduce the sentence imposed while maintaining conviction.

entities.text: Unnikrishnan Vs. State of Kerala; 2018 (15) SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. On a perusal of the aforesaid pronouncements by Hon'ble the Apex Court and unequivocal language of Sub-Clause 9 of Section 320 of Cr.P.C., it is apparent that offences which are not compoundable 6 CRR-3058-2024 in two tables of Section 320 of Cr.P.C., cannot be compounded.

However, Court can reduce the quantum of sentence while maintaining conviction.
14.
In view of the above settled position of law and on basis of compromise, a non-compoundable offence cannot be permitted to be compounded.

Consequently, compromise application (I.A.
No.19952 of 2024) being not maintainable is dismissed.
However, factum of compromise would be considered while considering the point of sentence.

15. List this case for final hearing on 25.11.2024.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE @shish Pankaj Hada vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128596002/
